sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) Languages: A Study from the Perspectives of Shared Innovation and Phylogenetic Estimation. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: online with a Harvard login (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Sani entry: 'it has 44 initials, 19 finals, and 5 tones (/55/, /44/, /33/, /2/, and /11/) (cf. TBL 1992: 667-8)'; comparative initial/final tables. The word 'stress' does not occur in the dissertation.

sources.citation: Grambank v1 (on file: sani1269 coded by JY from 'Ma 1951: in passim' only.
sources.note: Confirms Ma 1951 is the sole description used by Grambank; no prosodic features.

sources.citation: Bi Xian 毕贤. 2026. 石林撒尼彝语基数词变调研究 [Research on the Transposition of Base Number Words in Shilin Sani Yi Language]. 现代语言学 Modern Linguistics 14(8): 811-817. doi:10.12677/ml.2026.148845
sources.note: Silent on stress (no 重音/轻声/韵律 anywhere). Sec. 2 compares the Shilin Sani phoneme systems of Ma 1951 (44 initials, 19 finals, 5 tones 55/44/33/11/2), Kong 2002 (41/16/5 tones, short tone 2 > 31) and Zhou 2013 (41 initials, 31 finals, 3 tones 55/33/21); sec. 3 describes numeral tone sandhi 55+33 > 33+33, 55+55 > 33+55 conditioned by the following syllable's tone.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (zh) 撒尼语; Wikipedia (fr) Yi sani; Wikipedia (en) Sani language (read via MediaWiki API, 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Secondary. zh gives Laohaiyi (Shilin) inventory and 5 tones 55/44/33/11/31 citing Ma 1951 and Kong 2002; fr gives 4 tones citing Kong 2002 p. 22. No stress statement in any.

sources.citation: Iwasa, Kazue. 2022. An Overview of Negation in the Yi Languages -- Geolinguistic analysis of Yi character maps and a preliminary report on negation in Sani Yi. Grammatical Phenomena of Sino-Tibetan Languages 5: 85-104. Kyoto University.
sources.note: Only a general remark (p. 86): the Yi languages 'are tonal and basically open-syllabic except for loan words from Chinese'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Iwasa, Kazue 岩佐一枝. 2021. A Preliminary Report on Entomological Vocabulary in Sani Yi. Journal of Research Institute (Kobe City University of Foreign Studies) 61: 85-108.
sources.note: Silent on stress. Footnote 6 (p. 88) summarises Vial (1909: (5)-(8)) phonology: consonant and vowel letters and five tones ('first tone... clearly high'... 'fifth tone... clearly low'); fn. 15 notes a tone/vowel-constriction tendency (33 vs 44, 21 vs 31). Own fieldwork Shilin/Kunming 2019.

sources.citation: Iwasa, Kazue. 2019. 撒尼彝語の使役表現について [On causative expressions in Sani Yi]. In: Grammatical Phenomena of Sino-Tibetan Languages 2: Aspects of Causative Construction, 149-162. Kyoto University. hdl:2433/245171
sources.note: No phonology sketch; nothing on stress (data from Wukeshu village 五棵樹村, Shilin).

sources.citation: Ostapirat, Weera. 1996. Sani's Fortis See-Saw and initial devoicing. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 19(1): 59-64. doi:10.15144/LTBA-19.1.59
sources.note: Historical phonology of Sani initials/tones from Ma 1951 data (image PDF, scanned). No statement on Sani word stress; only a closing speculation (p. 63) that Tai/Cantonese kept codas 'due to their final stress'.

sources.citation: Vial, Paul. 1898. Les Lolos: histoire, religion, moeurs, langue, écriture. Shanghai: Imprimerie de la Mission catholique (Études sino-orientales, fasc. A). [data = dialecte gni, i.e. Sani]
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Ch. III 'De la langue des Lolos' (pp. 13-15) treats syllable shape (CV, no codas) and word order; tone is mentioned only in passing (p. 14 negative ma 'au second ton'; pp. 39-40 'le même mot ba pourra se prononcer sur le ton haut, bas, bref ou long'; p. 66 'je n'ai marqué aucun ton... il faut bien faire attention aux accents' where 'accents' = French diacritics on vowels, not stress).

sources.citation: Vial, Paul. 1909. Dictionnaire français-lolo, dialecte gni... province du Yunnan. Hongkong: Imprimerie de la Société des Missions-Étrangères. Grammar pp. (1)-(103), phonology pp. (5)-(8).

sources.note: The only full grammar (Glottolog 'grammar', 371 pp.; basis of Grambank, STEDT, Bradley 1979, Ostapirat 1996). Its 语音 chapter (声母/韵母/声调/连读变调) is the place where any 轻重音/重音 remark would be; nobody in the accessible literature reports what it says on stress.
